accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE (2013) science programme of study (Y1 basic parts of the human body; Y3 skeletons and muscles for support, protection and movement), NHS and KidsHealth pages on bones and muscles, and Gray's Anatomy basics: about 206 bones in an adult and roughly 270 to 300 at birth that fuse; skull protects the brain, ribcage the heart and lungs, spine supports the body and guards the spinal cord; skeletal muscles attach by tendons and only contract, working in antagonistic pairs (biceps flexes, triceps extends the elbow); the heart is cardiac muscle; most people have 12 pairs of ribs. The arm picture is labelled front and back muscle rather than overstating anatomy.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented primary misconceptions about the skeleton (Osborne, Wadsworth and Black 1992 SPACE report; Reiss and Tunnicliffe 2001 children's drawings of the inside of the body): bones are a few loose pieces or one bone (challenge onebone and head, m1), body would be unchanged without bones (step 1 prediction, p1), muscles push (step 4 prediction, p5, m3, challenge push), bones move themselves (challenge self), organs placed in the wrong cage (step 3 feedback, challenge ribs, spine, skull, legs) and the heart is a bone because it sits in the ribcage (sort card, m4, challenge heartbone and cage).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbones is about the skeleton's three jobs and how muscles move bones: the body squashes into a puddle when the bones are removed, a five-piece skeleton build on a body outline with region hit tests, organ-guard matching, and a jointed arm whose front muscle shortens and bulges while bending and whose back muscle pulls it straight. flagbody names outside body parts for ages 2 to 3 and flagheart pumps blood through vessels; neither has a skeleton, organ protection or an antagonistic muscle pair. lab_distinct gate is under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each idea before the text states it: the body flops only when the bones come out, a wrong place for the skull or ribcage is refused with where it really goes, the leg bones are refused as a guard for the heart, and in the arm step the label switches from front muscle pulls to back muscle pulls the moment the hand changes direction, so the task can only finish by using both muscles. The done message for each task then names the idea.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then tests: 'Just the same' without bones (the body flops), 'To help you hear' for the skull (the guard step places the skull over the brain), and 'It pushes the bone' for bending (the front muscle shortens and pulls, and a second muscle is needed to straighten). Each reveal line restates which option was right.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions, every wrong option tagged with one of twelve distinct messages: bones pump blood, bones pull, the ribcage or spine guarding the brain, the skull or leg bones guarding the heart, muscles push, bones move by themselves, the skeleton as one bone, the skeleton as only head bones, the heart as a bone and the heart as a cage. Each names the slip in child words and restates the fact.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 0.7 and adult at 9.5 (family limits 5.0 and 10.0). Kid sentences are short and concrete (Your skull is like a hard helmet; Bend your arm and feel the front of it go hard). Canvas labels are two to six words, for example 'Bone 1 of 5', 'Drag the hand', 'No bones: floppy!'. Key words in the adult text use the curriculum terms skeleton, skull, ribcage, spine, joint, support, protect.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea: the skeleton gives shape, bones protect, muscles pull, muscles only pull and the heart is a muscle. Items spread over support (p1), protection (p3, m2, m6), the skeleton as a whole (m1, p4, m9), muscles pulling (p2, p5, m3, m7, m8), the heart as a muscle (m4) and ribs in pairs (m5) with no repeated stems.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android screenshots in light and dark, plus 1200 px desktop, for every step at the start, mid Show me and end: the squashed body stays inside the canvas with the small Bones out skeleton beside it, the bone card sits top right above the outline with the step counter clear of it, the three guard tiles fit across the bottom, the jointed arm uses most of the width with the hand, Elbow and status labels readable, and the sort card and two trays fit with their counts. Body outline was lightened in dark theme after the first dark check.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Take the bones out or Put the bones back, five place buttons per bone, three guard buttons per organ, Bend the arm and Straighten the arm, and Bone or Muscle per card. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with what happened and why. walk.cjs runs every task with Show me and axe WCAG 2.1 AA in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
